meta.note: Compiled from primary statistical sources where available (EIA, Eurostat, GIIGNL, China customs, Gassco, Norwegian Offshore Directorate, World Nuclear Association) and from Kpler, Vortexa, S&P Global and AXS Marine ship-tracking figures as quoted in trade press. Most flows are calendar 2025, the last full year before the 2026 Strait of Hormuz closure, so the map shows the pre-crisis baseline; a few coal and uranium flows are 2024. Chokepoint totals are EIA first-half 2025 averages. The Energy Institute Statistical Review 2026 trade tables could not be retrieved, so several crude and product flows are importer-side or tracker-based and definitions differ (customs versus tanker tracking, EU versus all Europe, crude versus total products including LPG). Flows are selected major routes, not an exhaustive or additive trade matrix, and hub pairs sometimes stand for wider regions as described in each note. Confidence: high = taken directly from a primary table, medium = single secondary source or simple derivation, low = rounded estimate with the derivation given in the note. Uranium bilateral trade is opaque and those figures are indicative only. Conversions: 7.33 bbl per tonne of crude, 10.34 bcm/yr per Bcf/d.

hubs.name: Russia Far East (Kozmino/ESPO, Sakhalin, Power of Siberia)

chokepoints.name: Strait of Hormuz
chokepoints.lng_note: LNG 11.4 Bcf/d in 1H25 (about a fifth of world LNG trade), mostly Qatar; about one-third of China's LNG passes here
chokepoints.note: 1H25 average (2024: 20.7; EIA quarterly 4Q25: 21.6). 74% of crude went to China, India, Japan and Korea. Effectively closed from about 1 March 2026 after US-Israel strikes on Iran: EIA shows 14.9 mb/d in 1Q26 and 4.9 mb/d in 2Q26, so 2025 volumes are the pre-crisis baseline.

chokepoints.name: Strait of Malacca
chokepoints.note: 1H25 average (2024: 22.5); largest oil chokepoint, about 29% of seaborne oil trade. Fell to 16.6 mb/d in 2Q26 as the Hormuz closure cut Gulf supply to Asia.

chokepoints.name: Suez Canal and SUMED Pipeline
chokepoints.lng_note: LNG 0.9 Bcf/d in 1H25, down from 4.1 in 2023
chokepoints.note: 1H25 average (2024: 4.8; 2023: 8.8). Flows roughly halved after Houthi attacks in the Red Sea from late 2023 pushed tankers around the Cape; partial recovery to 5.9 mb/d by 4Q25.

chokepoints.name: Bab el-Mandeb
chokepoints.lng_note: LNG 0.0 Bcf/d in 2024 and 1H25 (4.2 in 2023): LNG carriers avoid the route entirely
chokepoints.note: 1H25 average (2024: 4.1; 2023: 9.3). Red Sea rerouting after Houthi attacks; EIA shows a rebound to 5.4 mb/d in 4Q25 and 8.1 mb/d in 2Q26.

chokepoints.name: Turkish Straits (Bosporus and Dardanelles)
chokepoints.lng_note: LNG 0.6 Bcf/d via the Dardanelles (to Marmara terminals); no LNG transits the Bosporus
chokepoints.note: 1H25 Dardanelles figure (Bosporus alone: 3.3; 2024 Dardanelles: 3.6). Carries Russian Black Sea and Kazakh CPC crude; CPC terminal and tankers were hit by drone attacks in 2025.

chokepoints.name: Danish Straits
chokepoints.note: 1H25 average (2024: 4.9; 2021: 3.1). Volumes rose after 2022 as Russian Baltic crude was redirected from European pipelines and nearby buyers to long-haul shipments to India and China; shadow-fleet scrutiny is the main current risk.

chokepoints.name: Panama Canal
chokepoints.lng_note: LNG below 0.3 Bcf/d in FY2025, down from about 2.5 Bcf/d in FY2021
chokepoints.note: Fiscal year 2025 (FY2024: 2.0). Almost all products and LPG (2.2 of 2.3 mb/d), mainly US Gulf Coast to Asia and Pacific South America. The 2023-24 drought cut transits; US LNG has not returned to the route.

chokepoints.name: Cape of Good Hope
chokepoints.note: 1H25 average (2024: 9.3; 2023: 6.2). Not a true chokepoint but the main bypass: volumes jumped about 50% when Red Sea traffic rerouted in 2024.

flows.note: Kpler: Middle East was about 52% (about 1.9bn of 3.6bn barrels) of China's 2025 seaborne crude. Believed to include Iranian crude (about 1.38 mb/d per Kpler), which China customs records as Malaysian or Indonesian; treat as approximate.
Derived: Kpler total imports about 4.8 mb/d times a Middle East share of about 44% (Iraq, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait monthly shares in 2025). No full-year bilateral figure found.
Japanese government figures: 2.22 of 2.36 mb/d total imports (94%) came from the Middle East, mainly UAE and Saudi Arabia.
KNOC data: 69.9% of 2.80 mb/d total imports, a three-year low share.

EU only: Eurostat 55.9 Mt (13.0% of 429.3 Mt EU crude imports), led by Saudi Arabia 29.6 Mt and Iraq 25.1 Mt; converted at 7.33 bbl/t. Part moves via Yanbu/SUMED or the Cape rather than Bab el-Mandeb.
EIA Persian Gulf origin total; Saudi Arabia 0.27, Iraq 0.18. Much of it lands on the US West Coast.

China customs: Russia 17.4% of 578 Mt (about 100.6 Mt), down 6.9% y/y. Includes ESPO pipeline (about 0.6-0.7 mb/d), Kozmino seaborne and Urals/Arctic cargoes from western ports, plus 0.2 mb/d transiting Kazakhstan.

Kpler: about 1.70 mb/d average in 2025 (1.78 in 2024), roughly 35% of India's imports. Mostly Urals from Baltic and Black Sea ports; fell sharply from December 2025 after US sanctions on Rosneft and Lukoil.

Urals averaged about 275 kb/d in 2025 (Reuters); Kpler shows 317 kb/d of all Russian crude in Jan-Oct. Not drawn: about 0.19 mb/d (2.2% of EU imports) still reaching Hungary and Slovakia via the Druzhba pipeline.

Estimate: about 400 kb/d of jet (Kpler, May-Sep 2025) plus roughly 100 kb/d of diesel. No full-year figure found; flows fell to near zero after the 2026 Hormuz closure.
